skill.name: executing-plans
skill.description: Guides agents through written implementation plans using critical review, batched execution, verification, and feedback checkpoints.
skill.summary: Execute written plans in batches with review checkpoints and verification.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the prompt-only skill. Manual review found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unsafe executable behavior.

content.value_statement: Written plans can fail when agents rush into unclear steps. This skill adds review, batched execution, verification, and feedback checkpoints.
actual_capabilities: Reviews a written plan before work begins.
Raises concerns before executing unclear or risky steps.
Executes plan tasks in small batches.
Tracks task progress from in progress to completed.
Reports implemented work and verification output between batches.
Stops for clarification when blockers or repeated failures appear.
limitations: Requires a written plan before it can guide execution.
Does not create the initial implementation plan.
Does not replace human review at checkpoints.
Depends on available verification commands and project context.

use_cases.title: Plan Execution for Developers
use_cases.description: Use a reviewed implementation plan to complete code changes in controlled batches.

use_cases.title: Checkpoint Reviews for Tech Leads
use_cases.description: Keep agents aligned with architecture decisions before more tasks are started.

use_cases.title: Verified Delivery for Project Maintainers
use_cases.description: Require verification output and progress reports before approving the next batch.

prompt_templates.title: Execute a Simple Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executing-plans skill with this plan file. Review it first, then execute the first batch with verification.

prompt_templates.title: Review Before Starting
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executing-plans skill. Read the plan, list any concerns, and wait if the plan has blocking gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Batch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executing-plans skill to complete the next three tasks. Report changes and verification output before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Execute with Strict Checkpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the executing-plans skill for this implementation plan. Stop on blockers, verify each task, and request review between batches.

output_examples.input: Execute the first three tasks from my implementation plan.
output_examples.output: The agent reviews the plan, completes the first batch, runs verification, and reports results for feedback.

output_examples.input: Continue after reviewer feedback on the previous batch.
output_examples.output: The agent applies requested changes, starts the next batch, and pauses again after verification.

output_examples.input: The verification command fails twice during a task.
output_examples.output: The agent stops execution, reports the blocker, and asks for clarification instead of guessing.

best_practices: Provide a clear plan file with small, verifiable tasks.
Review concerns before allowing implementation to begin.
Check verification output before approving the next batch.
anti_patterns: Starting execution before reading the full plan.
Skipping verification because a change looks simple.
Continuing through repeated failures without asking for help.

faq.question: Does this skill write an implementation plan?
faq.answer: No. It helps execute an existing written plan with review and checkpoints.

faq.question: How many tasks are executed at once?
faq.answer: The default first batch is three tasks, unless the user gives different guidance.

faq.question: What happens when the plan has problems?
faq.answer: The agent raises concerns before starting work and waits when the gaps are blocking.

faq.question: Does it require verification commands?
faq.answer: It expects verification when the plan or project provides suitable checks.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: When should the agent stop?
faq.answer: It should stop for unclear instructions, missing dependencies, blockers, or repeated verification failures.
